items.title: Wormholes are 'FAKE'
items.text:
Honestly i’m tired of seeing these "scientists" on the internet trying to sell us on wormholes. They take a piece of paper, fold it, poke a pencil through it and say "look! a shortcut!" it’s a joke. they are thinking like 2d creatures living on a flat sheet. we live in a 3d world created by the CREATOR and you cant just "fold" the fabric of space because you found a glitch in a math equation.
as a hardware guy i look at the actual build. a black hole isn't a "doorway" or some magic portal. it’s a singularity. it’s a solid dot of super massive mass. in 3d reality you can’t have a hole inside a single point. it’s a physical dead end. it’s a crusher, not a tunnel.
i think these people are just child minded. they spend all day staring at equations and forget to check the reality outside. or maybe they just want the millions of views and the fame that comes with selling a fantasy. they try to distract people from the truth by making up these imaginary "shortcuts" through the 4th dimension.
at the end of the day, math is just paperware. it doesn’t mean it works in the real hardware of the universe. they are just chasing fairy tales and call it science to get clicks. there is no hole in the space-time, only the divine order of the Creator.

items.title: Gravity may not be what we think of it is.
items.text: We tend to look at space as an empty vacuum, but it’s far from it—it’s packed with dark matter and dark energy. At a fundamental level, everything has inertia; an inherent, stubborn resistance to being moved. When mass exists in space, it interacts with this inertia like an object being pushed into an elastic cloth. The cloth resists and builds up potential energy, wanting to push the object right back out. But mass can't be thrown out of space-time because space-time is everywhere, and mass and energy are just two faces of the exact same thing. Gravity isn't just a pull; it’s the result of mass forcing its way into a universe that stubbornly wants to stay still, creating a tension that can never be escaped.

items.title: Take a look you'll found something even it's looking completely empty!
items.text:
I don’t really like studying Biology, but to be honest, without it I might not be here. And it’s not only about me—it’s the same for you and every living creature! This hateful subject (according to me) sometimes really amazes me. In this article, I’m gonna show you exactly why!

There are so many species of living things you won’t even believe it unless you explore it yourself. It's true that if we read something like “there are ‘x’ number of species ever discovered,” it sounds normal until you start looking at the details!!

Every species has its own way of life. Even if they are from the same family, they are not the same; they have something a bit special about them, just like us humans. You, who are reading this, I don’t know who you are, but think about it: you and I both are humans, or scientifically speaking, Homo sapiens. Even if it’s a coincidence that we kinda look similar, we are not the same. We are different somewhere, we have our own destiny, and our fundamental memory—our DNA—is different.

Just like that, there is a very unique kind of species known as the salamander, which is a type of amphibian.

There are a lot of types of them. Salamanders are something really unique!! You can even call some of them “Aliens.” Wondering why?



The image shown above demonstrates a few types of salamanders (and yes, to answer your wonder, there are actually over 700 different species of them!).

To understand why most people call them aliens, you need to take a look at their abilities. There is a salamander known as the “Axolotl”—you probably have seen this in Minecraft, right? These creatures can regenerate almost any damaged part of their body, just about anything!! Crazy, right?? Even neurons!!!

Then there is another salamander known as the “Olm.” People literally call it a Pokémon! It has no eyes, it moves by sensing its surroundings, and it can survive for up to 10 years without any touch of food. It can be found in dark, underwater caves.
